kind: research protocol and GPU experiment program

runtime.execution: External coding agent edits a Python training program and launches separate GPU processes; repo contains no autonomous provider loop.
runtime.service_boundary: Consumes an externally supplied agent/GPU environment; does not supply harness/provider/service ownership.

summary: A narrow, explicit edit/run/measure/keep protocol with a fixed evaluator is useful for autodroit, but its agent governance is authored instructions.

inspection.scope: Read full program instructions, README role, train timing/failure/eval loop and bits-per-byte evaluator.
inspection.limits: No GPU training, agent invocation or benchmark reproduction; no authored agent engine or test suite in snapshot.

actions.name: edit/commit/run/measure/keep/discard loop

actions.name: train.py

actions.output: Training log and printed BPB/VRAM/time metrics
actions.lifecycle: One GPU process, measured five-minute training budget excludes warmup.

actions.name: evaluate_bpb
actions.lifecycle: After candidate training; no harness activation.
actions.authority: Fixed evaluator calls editable model loss

authority.detail: Protocol authorizes autonomous edits inside one file after initial setup; library/evaluator restrictions are instructions, not enforcement.

evaluation.detail: BPB against held validation data and crash/time rules provide an external metric; evaluator trusts editable model loss behavior, not a harness correctness TCK.

time_order.detail: Training budget accumulates time.time deltas after warmup with CUDA synchronization; operator kill deadline is host instruction and wall-clock jumps are not handled here.

evidence.claim: Editable train.py and read-only prepare.py/evaluation constraints; baseline first, metric and simplicity selection.
External agent commits candidate, runs to log, reads metric, records TSV and keeps/resets; ten-minute kill is an instruction.
Training loops with CUDA synchronization, NaN/loss fast-fail and measured budget excluding warmup.
BPB computes loss per target byte over validation tokens with fixed sequence length; editable model produces per-token loss.
Final printed metric, time, VRAM, tokens and model shape feed external selection.

strengths: Tiny editable surface and explicit fixed measurement make experimental progress intelligible.
Keep/discard/crash vocabulary records unsuccessful experiments as part of research.
limits: No agent runtime, continuous self-hosted refit or invariant-preserving oracle supplied.
Fixed prepare.py does not prevent a malicious/incorrect editable model from returning misleading loss; scientific score is narrower than system correctness.
arconaut_questions: How can autodroit keep model-directed experiment freedom while retaining independent fault-class oracles and failed attempts?
Which experiment objective is external to the changing harness and cannot be silently altered by it?
